title: Running from the law ; Attempted murder sparks police chase that ends in driver being shot
article: Rainer Elsner lumbered through branches along a dirt path to his neighbour's house after he was shot in the head, back and arm in his Carp-area home.

He was turning white from shock, and even though Jean-Claude Hubert insisted he come inside, Elsner didn't want to make a mess in his friend's home. Hubert asked his wife to call police and he tended to Elsner on the deck.
The 911 call launched a dinner-hour chase Wednesday on Hwy. 417 that ended with a man shot by Ottawa police and the arrival of the Ontario Special Investigations Unit.
Elsner, a 65-year-old denturist who works out of his longtime home on Bear Hill Rd., told Hubert he was allegedly shot by an employee.

According to the account Elsner gave Hubert, the employee allegedly drove to Elsner's bungalow to talk about "the money," which Elsner suspected someone stole while he was on a recent trip to Germany.
Elsner told Hubert a glass window was smashed and shots rang out.
Elsner escaped through his back door and, looking for refuge, ended up in his neighbour's backyard as Hubert, 68, was firing up his barbecue for dinner.
"He came through the yard screaming, 'I've been shot!' " Hubert said yesterday.
Although Elsner was injured and emotionally shaken, he was able to relay details to police and Lanark paramedics.
As paramedics transported Elsner to hospital, police broadcast a description of a suspect's car and soon found a vehicle matching that description travelling eastbound on Hwy. 417 near Parkdale Ave.
Cops intercepted the vehicle near Walkley Rd. and there was a brief standoff between the driver and officers.
Police shot the 28-year-old man in the chest and paramedics transported him to Ottawa Hospital's Civic campus.
Richard Bastien, who is engaged to be married, was last reported in critical condition and on life-support yesterday.
SIU spokesman Frank Phillips couldn't say whether the police shooting victim fired first or if a gun was found at the scene.
"Something caused that officer to discharge his firearm and I don't know what. That's what we need to find out," Phillips said.
Witnesses to the Hwy. 417 shooting said a police cruiser appeared to have several bullet holes in the windshield.
The SIU is questioning one subject officer and two witness officers.
Police closed the highway's eastbound lanes around Walkley Rd. area until 8:30 a.m. yesterday.

Back on Bear Hill Rd., detectives were treating Elsner's shooting as an attempted murder. Part of the investigation is determining what kind of gun shot Elsner, possibly a low-powered firearm or pellet gun.

Those who know the employee said he was commuting from the Montreal area and had been working in Elsner's dental lab part-time for the past six years. They said Elsner had caught and confronted him about allegedly forging company cheques.
Elsner, described by Hubert as a "good neighbour," was listed in fair condition yesterday afternoon.
Clients were worried about Elsner's health when they heard what happened. Roger McGetchie said Elsner is "a great guy" who loves to golf and travel.
